tasks.title: Academic Discussion
tasks.instruction:
Your professor is teaching a class. Write a post responding to the professor's question.
In your response, you should do the following:
• Express and support your personal opinion.
• Make a contribution to the discussion in your own words.
An effective response will contain at least 100 words.

professor.name: Dr. Gupta
professor.text: We've been discussing how consumer purchasing decisions affect environmental outcomes. Some economists believe that people should prioritize buying products that last longer and can be repaired, even if they cost more initially, because this reduces manufacturing waste and resource consumption. Others argue that people should prioritize buying newer products with advanced energy-efficient technologies, even if they replace items more frequently, because modern innovations significantly reduce daily environmental impact. Which purchasing strategy do you think produces better environmental outcomes?

posts.name: Kelly
posts.text: I believe prioritizing durable, repairable products produces better environmental outcomes even when they cost more initially. When people buy high-quality goods like long-lasting electronics and well-made clothing, they reduce the demand for frequent manufacturing and prevent tons of waste. This purchasing strategy also supports companies that design products responsibly rather than those focused only on planned obsolescence and profit maximization.

posts.name: Andrew
posts.text: I think buying newer products with advanced, energy-efficient technologies produces better environmental outcomes despite more frequent replacement. Modern appliances, vehicles, and electronics use significantly less energy than older models, reducing daily carbon emissions and resource consumption. The environmental savings from using highly efficient technology for several years often outweigh the manufacturing costs of producing newer, cleaner products more frequently.
